report.answer_text:
Sanae Takaichi became prime minister in October 2025. Her main economic proposals that year were these:
Stimulus package (approved Nov. 21, 2025)
Her Cabinet approved a ¥21.3 trillion ($136 billion) stimulus package.[1] It includes ¥17.7 trillion of spending, ¥2.7 trillion in tax breaks and ¥900 billion in special account spending.[1] It is the largest since the pandemic.[1]
It was built around three priorities. The first is relief from the rising cost of living. The second is "strategic investments" in shipbuilding, AI and semiconductors. The third is higher defense spending, bringing total defense expenditure to 2% of GDP.[2]
The inflation relief measures include scrapping a provisional gasoline tax and expanding subsidies for electricity and gas bills.[3]
It must be funded by a supplementary budget that parliament has to approve by the end of the year.[4]
"Responsible proactive fiscal policy"
This is her own name for her approach, which favors big fiscal spending.[5] She argued that financial sustainability is secured if debt grows more slowly than the economy.[6]
She said the aim is to strengthen national power through expansionary "wise spending" and to avoid excessively contractionary policies.[4]
Growth strategy
She announced a Growth Strategy Council to map out policies for innovation, industrial revitalization and "crisis management investments" in areas such as food security.[6]
She also reiterated commitments to making Japan a leading global asset management hub and to creating a national disaster-prevention agency.[6]
Monetary policy
A draft outline of the package urged the Bank of Japan to focus on strong growth with stable prices. That reflects her preference for low interest rates.[7]
Reception
Her approach has drawn comparisons to Abenomics.[8]
The package raised fears about Japan's large debt, pushing government bond yields to record highs and the yen lower against the dollar.[9]
Opposition lawmakers and experts have questioned whether it will be effective.[4]
